3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Earlier in the day, I learned that Frens Ricter's complaint had been accepted by the Supreme Court for review.

6.speaker: Livia Suno
6.text: "Sorry to interrupt, Mr. President, but Justice Garaci is here to see you."

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: I called Chief Justice Hawker's office to demand an explanation, but he wasn't in. I sat by the phone, waiting for him to call back.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: I had also been hearing countless reports about our police forces becoming reluctant to enforce the rules of the emergency.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: Suddenly, I heard a knock on the door.

11.speaker: Player
11.text: "I told you that I'm expecting an important call. No visitors."

12.speaker: Player
12.text: "I'm waiting for Orso Hawker, not Heron."

13.speaker: Livia Suno
13.text: "He told me that he's here to talk to you about the Emergency Act. He said he couldn't speak on the phone."

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: She opened the door for Heron Garaci and closed the door behind her.

19.speaker: Heron Garaci
19.text: "Hello, Mr. President. Sorry to have come unannounced, but I'm sure you expected us."

20.speaker: Narrator
20.text: Heron brushed past Livia and strode into the office. Livia gave me an apologetic half-smile, turned and closed the door behind her.

21.speaker: Heron Garaci
21.text: "It would be wise of you not to be so rude to your partners in the Court."

22.speaker: Heron Garaci
22.text: "I'm sorry if I disappointed you, but the Chief Justice is very busy."

23.speaker: Player
23.text: "Busy? I'm a busy man too, Mr. Garaci."

26.speaker: Player
26.text: "What is the Court plotting, Mr. Garaci?"

28.speaker: Heron Garaci
28.text: "Life is full of disappointments, Mr. President."

30.speaker: Heron Garaci
30.text: "We are not plotting anything, Mr. President. Please calm down."

31.speaker: Heron Garaci
31.text: "You already know that Frens Ricter has filed a complaint about your Emergency Act being unconstitutional. The judges couldn't ignore his arguments."

78.speaker: Heron Garaci
78.text: "We are simply a little disappointed about the lack of proper budget for our police and military forces. This Emergency Act has taken a heavy toll on them."

79.speaker: Heron Garaci
79.text: "And we have a few other suggestions that may help you manage this difficult period in the best way possible."

80.speaker: Heron Garaci
80.text: "We wish to see you address these concerns before the judicial review is concluded."

84.speaker: Heron Garaci

85.speaker: Heron Garaci
85.text: "Then I cannot promise the Court will find your actions constitutionally justified."

87.speaker: Heron Garaci

88.speaker: Heron Garaci

92.speaker: Heron Garaci

94.speaker: Heron Garaci
94.text: "We hope to see you revert your earlier decision to relax immigration laws with a decree as soon as possible."

101.speaker: Heron Garaci
101.text: "Our biggest concern, however, regards the Oligarchs. Walter Tusk and Marcel Koronti."

102.speaker: Heron Garaci
102.text: "They are in close cooperation with Arcasia and have ties to almost every other country on this continent. And as we all know, they only care about money."

103.speaker: Heron Garaci
103.text: "It is clear that they're trying to profit from the violence in Sordland and abroad. We have reason to believe they are supporting the militant organizations we are fighting against."

107.speaker: Heron Garaci

108.speaker: Heron Garaci

109.speaker: Heron Garaci

117.speaker: Heron Garaci

119.speaker: Heron Garaci
119.text: "Mr. President... You don't seem to understand the whole picture here."

120.speaker: Heron Garaci
120.text: "This is not only a matter of revoking the validity of your decree."

121.speaker: Heron Garaci
121.text: "As much as we're doing our best to help you out, the Court could still decide to try you for deliberately going against the Constitution."

122.speaker: Heron Garaci
122.text: "In the meantime, the Court will be doing its best. As long as you listen to our concerns, Chief Justice Hawker will be motivated to help you further..."

124.speaker: Heron Garaci
124.text: "With that said, they might be persuaded to rule in your favor if certain other judicial concerns were addressed."

126.speaker: Player

127.speaker: Player

128.speaker: Heron Garaci

129.speaker: Heron Garaci

130.speaker: Heron Garaci

131.speaker: Heron Garaci

132.speaker: Player

156.speaker: Heron Garaci

157.speaker: Heron Garaci
157.text: "Anyway, I am not here to argue with you."

158.speaker: Heron Garaci
158.text: "I hope our alliance stands strong. As I said earlier, there is nothing to worry about. The Court will reject Mr. Ricter's case..."

160.speaker: Heron Garaci
160.text: "Of course, there are some justices who believe you are to blame. Going against the Constitution is a serious offense, after all."

162.speaker: Player

172.speaker: Heron Garaci

174.speaker: Player

187.speaker: Heron Garaci

189.speaker: Heron Garaci
189.text: "Good. The Old Guard will be waiting."

190.speaker: Heron Garaci
190.text: "I have to say... You are not so different from President Alphonso."

193.speaker: Heron Garaci
193.text: "Well... For now, I must leave. I hope you'll think long and hard about what we just talked about."

197.speaker: Heron Garaci
197.text: "Goodbye, Mr. President. Thank you for your time."

242.text: Even if I was wrong, would I be able to get out of this if I wanted?

243.speaker: Narrator

262.speaker: Narrator
262.text: I had promised the people of Sordland that I would open our borders, and I had followed through. Turning back now would mean betraying all that work. On the other hand, so would losing the court case.

266.speaker: Narrator
266.text: Earlier in the day, I learned that Frens Ricter's complaint had been accepted by the Supreme Court for review.

267.speaker: Narrator
267.text: I had stopped the state of emergency, but the reformists and the Old Guard were still coming after me.

268.speaker: Narrator
268.text: I called Chief Justice Hawker's office to demand an explanation, but he wasn't in. I sat by the phone, waiting for him to call back.

272.speaker: Heron Garaci
272.text: "To be honest, Mr. Ricter has made a very compelling case against the Emergency Act. It's going to be very hard for us to refute it."

273.speaker: Heron Garaci
273.text: "Of course, there are some Justices who believe you were to blame from the beginning. Going against the Constitution was an impeachable offence, after all."

275.speaker: Heron Garaci
275.text: "This is having very negative effects on Sordland, Mr. President. You were supposed to use the state of emergency to its full advantage, not trigger more dissent by attacking militants and retreating before defeating them..."

276.speaker: Player

278.speaker: Heron Garaci

294.speaker: Heron Garaci

295.speaker: Heron Garaci

337.text: And then there was the conscription issue...

338.speaker: Narrator
338.text: If I reversed my policy, boys like my own son would be forced to join the army. Would I be able to live with that?

339.speaker: Player_Italic
339.text: Start working on a decree to reinstate conscription.

340.speaker: Player_Italic
340.text: Leave the law as it is.

341.speaker: Narrator
341.text: I didn't even want to think about Heron's demands for the Oligarchs. Nationalizing Sordland's two largest private corporations would have huge repercussions.

354.text: "You must reverse your ridiculous decision to end mandatory conscription. A large, strong military is the only way to ensure stability in this country."

356.speaker: Heron Garaci
356.text: "Do that and we will see about the rest."
